topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional local and systemic treatment modalities alongside the mechanisms responsible for treatment toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic genetic and signaling vulnerabilities unique to cancer cells.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule kinase inhibitors against driver oncogenes and managing the emergence of drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapeutics and drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the application of engineered antibodies to selectively target and deliver cytotoxic effects to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of immune surveillance and the clinical strategies used to mobilize and engineer T cells against tumors.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on broad clinical challenges, historical survival outcomes, and emerging paradigms in cancer management.
